current_answer: A real commercial expansion with uneven return expectations—not an empty financial system or a guarantee of satisfactory returns. Paid persistence and selected older-capacity contracts strengthen the operating case. The holder evidence now adds cash actually realized by an investor and capital able to absorb some losses. Yet a leveraged holder’s borrowing conditions can tighten before its equity is exhausted. The concern is not simply whether AI works, but whether enough net cash reaches each claim on terms its owner can finance. What the holder evidence changes.
summary: Real paid demand. Providers can retain value. Older capacity can earn again. Some gains have reached investors as cash—but the funding of the investor also matters.
uncertainty: For continuation, obtain the actual A100 term, deployment age and net service economics, plus Austin’s billed-to-collected fees and cash costs. Compare a documented refit with the best feasible continued use rather than assuming every expired contract requires a new generation. Decisive observations and their limits.
